h1: The 8 Best Printers with USB Ports of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best printers with USB ports, covering Canon, HP, Brother and Epson models that print from a wired computer.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TR8620a is the best USB printer here, with a USB-B port, auto feeder, fax and AirPrint support. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the strongest value for home offices, the Brother DCP-L2640DW suits laser fans, and the Epson XP-7100 is the one listing that names USB in writing.
intro: The word USB hides a trap. Almost every printer here has a square USB-B port for connecting to a computer, but that is not the flat USB-A slot you plug a flash drive into. Buyers who want the second one get the first.

We ranked eight printers on the listing details: the connection type, the office features around it, and how clearly the listing confirms the port. Note that several listings do not confirm a USB-A flash drive slot, so none are chosen for that.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A USB-B wired connection with a full home-office feature set.
products.description:
The TR8620a offers a USB-B port for a wired computer link, an auto document feeder, AirPrint and Android printing, and built-in fax, copy and scan. Cost runs $100-200.

Placement: it ranks first because it pairs the port with the widest office toolset on this list. The HP OfficeJet Pro below is cheaper but lists fewer mobile options.

Buy it if you want a dependable wired link plus real office tools. Caveat: it costs more than the budget models.
products.idealFor: Home offices that want a wired link and full toolset.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Feeder, duplex and a USB-B backup for under $100.
products.description:
The 8125e has a USB-B port for wired computer use, an automatic document feeder, duplex printing and a three-month Instant Ink trial. Cost runs $50-100.

Placement: it ranks second behind the Canon because it lacks that model's fax and its listed mobile support. In return, it costs noticeably less for the same feeder and duplex.

A strong fit for home office buyers. Caveat: a USB-A flash drive slot is not confirmed on the listing.
products.idealFor: Home offices wanting feeder and duplex cheaply.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A wired monochrome laser with no ink to dry out.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with a USB-B port, duplex printing, copy and scan, and Alexa support. Cost runs $200-500.

Placement: it ranks below the inkjets for price, though it avoids ink drying out during long idle spells. It prints in black only.

Pick it for text-heavy work. Caveat: it is the priciest option here, and a flash drive slot is not confirmed.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy printing that sits idle between jobs.

products.name: Canon MAXIFY MB2720 Wireless Color Photo Printer
products.verdict: A business-minded MAXIFY with a USB-B link and fax.
products.description:
The MB2720 offers a USB-B port, scanner, copier and fax, plus color photo printing, in a business-oriented MAXIFY design. Cost runs $100-200.

Placement: it ranks fourth because the TR8620a gives you a feeder and mobile support in the same price band. The MB2720's strength is its office pedigree.

Suits small offices needing fax. Caveat: no flash drive slot is confirmed.
products.idealFor: Small offices that need fax over USB.

products.name: Epson Expression Premium XP-7100 Wireless Photo Printer, USB Connect
products.verdict: The only listing that names USB connectivity in writing.
products.description:
The XP-7100 names USB Connect directly on its listing and adds wireless duplex color photo printing, a scanner and copier, and mobile printing support. Cost runs $100-200.

Placement: it ranks fifth because it is photo-focused rather than office-focused, with no feeder listed. The explicit USB mention is its edge for buyers who want certainty.

Good for photo printing with a wired option. Caveat: it targets photos more than paperwork.
products.idealFor: Photo printers who want USB confirmed in writing.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Its small screen shows the connection status as you plug in.
products.description:
The TS6520 has a USB-B port, duplex printing and a compact body. Its small OLED screen reports the connection state, so you can see that the cable link is live.

It ranks sixth because it has no feeder and fewer office extras than the top picks. It does cost less than them.

Buy it if clear on-screen feedback matters. Caveat: a USB-A flash drive slot is not confirmed.
products.idealFor: Users who want visible confirmation of a wired link.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A low-cost USB-B printer with an automatic feeder.
products.description:
The TR4720 offers a USB-B port for wired use, an automatic document feeder and built-in fax, with wireless as well. Cost runs $50-100.

Placement: it ranks seventh because the HP 8125e offers the feeder plus duplex at a similar price. The fax is a legacy feature most buyers skip.

A reasonable wired backup on a tight budget. Caveat: no duplex is listed and flash drive support is unconfirmed.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a feeder and cable option.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Wireless first, with a plain USB-B port as a fallback.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 has a standard USB-B port, though wireless is the main way to connect. It includes a three-month Instant Ink trial and sits in the $50-100 bracket.

It ranks last because USB is a side feature here, and the listing does not confirm a flash drive slot. It is the cheapest cable-capable option.

Fits budget buyers who want a cable fallback. Caveat: it is a basic model.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a cable fallback.

whatMatters.detail: USB-B is the square port that connects the printer to a computer. USB-A is the flat slot for flash drives. Most printers here only confirm USB-B, so check the listing if you want a drive slot.
A cable avoids wifi drops and setup. It matters for a desktop that sits next to the printer. Check that the cable is included or buy one separately.
A feeder scans stacks of paper automatically. It matters for office paperwork. Look for ADF in the title.
Automatic two-sided printing saves paper. It matters for reports. Check the title or bullets for duplex.
Lasers do not dry out when idle, while inkjets can. This matters if you print rarely. Check the printer type in the title.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the printer by the job it does most.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Color and photos, lower upfront cost. Canon, HP and Epson models here.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: No ink drying out, black only. The Brother DCP-L2640DW.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to an inkjet unless printing is rare and text-only.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A USB-B port and, if you want it, USB named in the listing.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson XP-7100 names USB Connect directly, and the Canon TR8620a lists USB-B.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want fax, mobile printing and a feeder, which the Canon TR8620a combines.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a cable fallback. The HP DeskJet 4355 is the cheapest.

faq.q: Do these printers have a USB flash drive slot?
faq.a: Listings do not confirm one. They list a USB-B port for a computer connection.

faq.q: Does a cable come in the box?
faq.a: Check the listing. Some bundles omit it, so you may need a standard USB-B printer cable.

faq.q: Is a wired printer worth it over wireless?
faq.a: A cable is more stable for a desktop beside the printer. Wireless suits shared use.

faq.q: How do I set up a USB printer?
faq.a: Install the driver from the maker's site, plug in the cable and select the printer in your settings.

faq.q: Do I need ink for the Brother laser?
faq.a: It uses toner rather than ink, which does not dry out when idle.
Yes. Each model here also lists wireless or mobile printing.

finalTake: The Canon PIXMA TR8620a is the strongest overall USB printer. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is better value if you skip fax. Choose the Brother for text-only work, and remember that USB-B is not a flash drive slot.
